title: The Odyssey Shatters Box Office Records With $264 Million Global Opening, Biggest Ever for Nolan
excerpt: Christopher Nolan's IMAX epic scores $124.5 million domestically and sets the biggest non-franchise Hollywood opening ever in India at ₹73 crore.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Odyssey opened with $264 million globally, breaking Nolan's previous record of $180.4 million.
  • In India, it earned ₹73 crore ($7.5 million), the biggest debut for a non-franchise Hollywood film.
  • The film received an A on CinemaScore and 97% on Rotten Tomatoes, appealing to younger audiences.
  • IMAX contributed $52 million globally, marking only the second film to exceed $50 million in IMAX openings.

Box office data from the article
  • The Odyssey opened to $264 million worldwide, shattering Nolan's previous record of $180.4 million set by Oppenheimer and $249 million by The Dark Knight Rises
  • India opening of ₹73 crore ($7.5 million) marks the biggest debut ever for a non-franchise Hollywood production in the country
  • The film earned an A on CinemaScore and 97% on Rotten Tomatoes, with half of US ticket buyers aged 18-34
  • IMAX contributed $52 million globally, making it only the second film to score a $50+ million IMAX debut

Christopher Nolan has done it again. His adaptation of Homer's ancient Greek epic, The Odyssey, has smashed box office records worldwide with a $264 million global opening weekend — the biggest of the filmmaker's career and a massive vindication of the $250 million gamble Universal Pictures placed on a three-hour, R-rated film about a man trying to get home from war.

Record After Record

The numbers are staggering. Domestically, The Odyssey earned $124.5 million, making it the biggest live-action opening of 2026 and the third-highest overall behind Toy Story 5 and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. It became the best opening ever for star Matt Damon, the fourth-best for an R-rated film of all time (trailing only the three Deadpool entries), and Universal's biggest R-rated opening ever.

Internationally, the $139.6 million haul beat The Dark Knight Rises' $131 million launch to become Nolan's best debut outside North America. The film now holds the record as Nolan's highest opening in 48 countries.

Critical and audience reception has been overwhelmingly positive: an A on CinemaScore, 97% on Rotten Tomatoes, and an 81% "definite recommend" rating on PostTrak. With no major wide release scheduled for next weekend, the film appears well positioned to cross $1 billion worldwide.
